title: Remove fields without an immediate job
trigger: Signup asks for job title, company size, phone, or address before any of them changes access or first value.
action: Map every required field to its immediate purpose. Remove optional enrichment from account creation and ask for it later at the feature that needs it; retain necessary identity, fraud, and billing information.
mechanism: Reducing avoidable effort can preserve momentum after the buyer has chosen an offer.
guardrail: Verify downstream service still works and do not silently make essential data optional.
measure: Signup completion and paid activation; later setup abandonment.

title: Recover existing accounts inside signup
trigger: A returning buyer enters an existing account email and receives a dead-end error.
action: Offer a safe sign-in or account-recovery route within the signup journey, preserving the selected offer. Use the authentication system's established disclosure rules rather than exposing account existence to arbitrary visitors.
mechanism: A recovery path turns a mistaken entry point into continued progress.
guardrail: Test account enumeration protections, return destinations, and recovery for each supported identity method.
measure: Recovered purchases; duplicate accounts and unauthorized disclosures.

title: Support password managers during registration
trigger: New users abandon password creation or repeatedly fail manual entry.
action: Use correct autocomplete attributes, allow paste, and keep password-manager suggestions usable. Show the real password requirements before submission rather than discovering one rejected rule at a time.
mechanism: Recognition and assisted entry can reduce memory burden and avoidable retries.
guardrail: Keep the actual authentication policy; do not weaken controls merely to shorten the form.
measure: Completed registrations; credential errors and recovery requests.

title: Offer a reversible email typo correction
trigger: Verification messages fail to arrive because a buyer mistyped their address.
action: After entry, suggest a likely domain correction such as 'Did you mean example.com?' and ask the buyer to accept or retain their address. Provide an edit-email path on the verification screen.
mechanism: A recoverable check can prevent a small typo from becoming an unexplained dead end.
guardrail: Never replace an address automatically; support legitimate uncommon domains and international addresses.
measure: Verified accounts per registration; incorrect address changes.

title: Explain verification delivery and resend state
trigger: Buyers repeatedly click resend or leave because the verification screen gives no useful status.
action: Show the masked destination, last send status, realistic resend availability, and an edit-address action. Explain what to do when a link expires and let a newer link invalidate older ones according to the auth policy.
mechanism: Visible progress and a clear recovery route can reduce uncertainty during a necessary wait.
guardrail: Avoid fabricated delivery confirmation and prevent resend abuse without trapping legitimate buyers.
measure: Verification completion; duplicate sends and support contacts.

title: Resume the intended task after verification
trigger: Email verification opens a generic dashboard and loses the selected plan or unfinished action.
action: Bind a validated return destination and offer selection to the signup session. After verification, restore a concise summary and continue toward the chosen task instead of asking the buyer to select everything again.
mechanism: Continuity protects the buyer's earlier commitment and reduces repeated decisions.
guardrail: Allowlist destinations and validate current offers server-side; never trust a URL as price authority.
measure: Verified-account-to-purchase conversion; wrong-offer incidents.

title: Connect social sign-in to existing identity
trigger: A buyer uses a social provider after previously creating a password account and lands in a second empty account.
action: Use the established identity-linking flow to connect verified identities only after appropriate proof. Explain the existing account route and retain the intended workspace or offer during that confirmation.
mechanism: A coherent identity reduces confusion and prevents apparent loss of earlier work.
guardrail: Do not merge accounts solely because unverified email strings match; verify ownership and tenant permissions.
measure: Recovered sign-ins and purchases; account-merger incidents.

title: Remember the chosen sign-in method
trigger: Returning users try several authentication buttons because they cannot remember how they joined.
action: Where appropriate, remember a non-sensitive local hint such as 'You last used Google' and emphasize that supported method without hiding alternatives. Provide a clear way to use another account or device.
mechanism: Recognition can replace an unnecessary recall task at the start of a purchase.
guardrail: Treat the hint as a convenience, not proof of identity; avoid exposing personal account details on shared devices.
measure: Successful return sign-ins; wrong-account and privacy complaints.

title: Match mobile input to the field
trigger: Mobile signup requires switching keyboards repeatedly or produces capitalization errors in email addresses.
action: Use appropriate input types, autocomplete, input modes, and capitalization settings for each actual field. Test autofill and the mobile keyboard's next/done behavior on the complete form.
mechanism: Reducing mechanical effort can keep attention on completing the decision.
guardrail: Retain visible labels and validation; input hints must not reject valid international names or addresses.
measure: Mobile signup completion; correction rate and inaccessible fields.

title: Validate after a meaningful input attempt
trigger: The form marks incomplete fields red while the buyer is still typing or provides errors only after a long submission.
action: Validate at sensible boundaries such as field blur or submission, then give a specific correction near the affected field. Confirm repaired errors without repeatedly interrupting every keystroke.
mechanism: Timely feedback can reduce frustration without making normal entry feel like failure.
guardrail: Test keyboard and screen-reader behavior; do not announce every transient typing state.
measure: Completed forms; repeated validation failures and abandonment.

title: Preserve valid entries after server errors
trigger: A temporary network or server failure empties the signup form.
action: Keep non-sensitive valid entries and the selected offer when submission fails. Explain whether an account was created and offer a safe retry or sign-in path, using server state to prevent duplicate creation.
mechanism: Preserved effort can prevent a recoverable failure from feeling like a restart.
guardrail: Do not persist passwords or sensitive fields insecurely; distinguish timeout uncertainty from confirmed rejection.
measure: Recovered registrations; duplicate accounts and data exposure.

title: Navigate directly to form corrections
trigger: A long signup form fails validation but the buyer cannot locate the remaining problem.
action: Provide a concise error summary linking to each invalid field, move focus appropriately after submission, and retain the user's completed answers. State the correction instead of an internal error code.
mechanism: A clear correction path reduces search effort at a moment of frustration.
guardrail: Ensure summary links, field associations, focus order, and localized messages work together.
measure: Successful resubmissions; keyboard completion and support requests.

title: Let buyers inspect the password they typed
trigger: Password mismatches or hidden typing errors repeatedly block registration.
action: Add an accessible show/hide password control with a clear current state. Keep the same value and focus when toggling, and expose requirements beside the field without demanding a second password entry unless necessary.
mechanism: Reducing uncertainty about a hidden input can prevent avoidable retries.
guardrail: Default to concealed entry and test shared-device use, screen readers, autofill, and actual security requirements.
measure: Password-step completion; accidental disclosure and login failures.

title: Provide a cross-device verification route
trigger: A magic link opened on a phone fails because signup began on a desktop.
action: Support the authentication provider's secure cross-device completion or an approved one-time-code alternative. Explain which device should continue and show a recoverable state on the original screen when verification finishes elsewhere.
mechanism: Removing a device mismatch can preserve a buyer's interrupted intention.
guardrail: Use expiring, single-use credentials and the supported provider flow; do not bypass account verification.
measure: Cross-device verification completion; expired-code and account-access incidents.

title: Show the real remaining signup steps
trigger: A multi-step account flow hides how much work remains before the buyer can start.
action: Label the actual stages, such as 'Account, verify email, payment,' and mark completed stages from real state. Explain optional steps and let users return without losing entries.
mechanism: A credible endpoint can reduce uncertainty about the required effort.
guardrail: Do not use fake completion percentages or conceal payment behind an apparently final signup step.
measure: Completed journeys; unexpected-step complaints and backtracking.

title: Route invitations into the invited workspace
trigger: An invited teammate signs up and accidentally creates a separate workspace.
action: Validate the invitation and show the inviter, intended workspace, role, and expiry before acceptance. After identity creation, join the permitted workspace instead of running the unrelated new-workspace wizard.
mechanism: A task-matched path makes the invitation's value immediately attainable.
guardrail: Verify invitation ownership and role authorization; do not expose private workspace details before access is established.
measure: Accepted invitations and team activation; orphan workspaces.

title: Resolve invitation email mismatches explicitly
trigger: A signed-in user opens an invitation intended for another email and sees a generic forbidden page.
action: Explain that the current identity cannot accept this invitation, then offer secure account switching or a request for a corrected invitation. Preserve the invitation context through the approved recovery route.
mechanism: A specific explanation can turn an authorization boundary into a solvable task.
guardrail: Do not transfer invitations automatically or disclose the intended recipient unnecessarily.
measure: Recovered invite acceptance; unauthorized memberships.

title: Explain identity-provider permissions at signup
trigger: Buyers hesitate at an identity consent screen because requested permissions seem unrelated to creating an account.
action: Use the minimum scopes supported by the signup task and explain the specific data needed immediately before the provider handoff. Request broader product access later when the user invokes that feature.
mechanism: A bounded request can make consent feel understandable and proportionate.
guardrail: Verify the displayed explanation matches actual scopes and preserve a supported alternate sign-in route.
measure: Provider consent completion; revoked access and privacy questions.

title: Clarify persistent sign-in on shared devices
trigger: The product serves people using public or shared computers, but persistent login is presented without explanation.
action: Offer an explicit persistent-session choice where the authentication system supports it, explain its effect in plain language, and make signing out discoverable. Keep a normal short-session route available.
mechanism: Control over session persistence can reduce a practical concern about joining or buying.
guardrail: Honor actual session lifetimes and security policy; do not imply a shared device is safe merely because a box is unchecked.
measure: Completed secure sign-ins; unintended persistent sessions.

title: Recover partially created accounts cleanly
trigger: Account creation succeeds but workspace provisioning fails, leaving users unsure whether to register again.
action: Show an accurate account-created state with provisioning progress, a safe retry, and a support reference. Let the user sign back into the same account and resume provisioning instead of creating another identity.
mechanism: A truthful intermediate state preserves progress and confidence after a backend interruption.
guardrail: Use idempotent provisioning and never display usable access before required resources exist.
measure: Provisioned accounts and paid activation; duplicate workspaces.
